title: India Inc. Just Beat Earnings Estimates for the Quarter. The Iran War May Erase the Gains.
excerpt: Nifty 50 companies posted 6.6% profit growth in the January-March quarter, well ahead of the 2% forecast. Mid-caps grew 35%. But elevated oil at $97 and a record foreign fund exodus threaten the quarters ahead.
body:
Indian companies have delivered a surprise earnings beat for the January-March quarter, powered by strong domestic consumption and easy monetary policy. But the celebration may be short-lived.

Net profit for Nifty 50 companies rose 6.6% year-on-year in the three months ended March 31, comfortably ahead of analyst forecasts that had projected just 2% growth, according to data compiled by Kotak Institutional Equities. It was the eighth consecutive quarter of single-digit profit growth for India's blue-chip universe — steady but unremarkable against the backdrop of the world's fastest-growing major economy.

## Who Drove the Numbers

Banks and financial companies shouldered much of the growth, benefiting from stable asset quality and improving credit demand. Metal producers rode rising global commodity prices, while oil marketing companies posted strong margins in a quarter that preceded the Iran war's full impact on crude prices.

Beyond the Nifty 50, the picture was more impressive. Nomura's broader universe of 256 companies recorded profit-after-tax growth of 18%, while Motilal Oswal's 359-company tracker delivered 16% growth. The real outperformance came from the middle of the market: mid-cap firms grew earnings by roughly 35%, and small-caps advanced nearly 20%, significantly outpacing their larger peers.

The consumer tax cuts introduced in the Union Budget provided a demand boost, particularly for automobile and fast-moving consumer goods companies. Telecom firms also improved after years of stress, helped by tariff hikes and industry consolidation.

## Where the Weakness Lives

The technology sector — India's largest white-collar employer and a bellwether for diaspora employment — posted tepid revenue growth. Mounting concerns over AI-driven disruption to traditional IT outsourcing models have cast a shadow over the sector, even as AI adoption has paradoxically begun driving new demand for software companies.

IT stocks rallied 7% in two sessions this week on commentary from global software companies indicating that AI adoption is driving broader demand. But American-listed shares of Infosys and Wipro dropped 2.5% and 8.3% respectively overnight on Tuesday, suggesting the rally may have overshot.

Pharmaceutical companies grappled with continued weakness in the US generics market, where pricing pressure shows no signs of easing. Cement, consumer staples and durable goods makers all showed pressure from rising raw material and freight costs — a harbinger of what elevated oil prices might do across the economy.

## The Iran War Cloud

The earnings beat is a rearward-looking number. The January-March quarter ended before the Iran war had fully disrupted global supply chains and before Brent crude settled above $90 a barrel.

Since then, the Strait of Hormuz blockade has cut off more than 40% of India's traditional oil import route. Foreign investors have sold Indian shares for three consecutive sessions, pulling out ₹83.63 billion ($878 million) on Tuesday alone, adding to their record selloff for the year. India has slipped to seventh in global market capitalisation rankings, overtaken by South Korea's AI chip-heavy market.

Domestic institutional investors bought ₹95.89 billion worth of shares on Tuesday, helping benchmarks snap a four-session losing streak. But analysts warn that domestic liquidity, while providing a buffer, cannot substitute for the clarity the market needs on geopolitics and energy prices.

## Forward Outlook

Analysts warn that the current quarter — April through June — will tell a very different story. Higher input costs from crude above $95, supply chain disruptions across chemicals and fertilisers, and the dampening effect of uncertainty on capital expenditure decisions all point to margin compression.

"While strong domestic liquidity is providing an important buffer, a more durable improvement in sentiment is likely to require greater clarity on the geopolitical front and a sustained easing in energy prices," said Ponmudi R, CEO of Enrich Money.

The Nifty 50 is expected to open flat on Wednesday, with GIFT Nifty futures at 23,474, indicating the index would hold near Tuesday's close of 23,483.55. With Brent crude at $97, the market is waiting for a signal that the worst is over. It has not received one yet.
nri_angle: For NRI investors with Indian market exposure through direct equities, mutual funds, or India-focused ETFs, the Q4 numbers confirm the domestic consumption story. But the IT sector's tepid revenue growth is relevant for diaspora tech workers who hold stock in Indian IT companies. The AI disruption narrative cuts both ways — threatening legacy outsourcing but potentially driving new demand for AI services.
author: Diaspora Desk
